title: Budgeted Batch Scheduler and Quant Profile Registry
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduces a budget-aware batch scheduler and a tenant-visible quantization profile registry. Adds simulation dry-run, shadow-run mode for safe rollout, telemetry hooks for unit-econ per-tenant, and a CLI command to export suggested defaults.
description:
Context and motivation: Tenant workloads vary wildly and our default batching/quantization heuristics have been conservative, leaving unit economics on the table for budget-conscious customers. This PR implements a Budgeted Batch Scheduler that respects tenant budget SLOs and a Quant Profile Registry to manage and safely roll out compact quantization profiles per tenant. The changes aim to reduce per-token cost while keeping tail latency SLAs.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces budgeted_batch_scheduler service: horizon-based prefill logic, budget windowing, tenant-level soft SLOs, and graceful fallback to standard scheduler when headroom is low. 2) Adds quant_profile_registry: stores named quant profiles (fp16, int8-ld, int8-zp-compact, q4f) with metadata (expected speedup, estimated quality delta), rollout states (shadow, canary, staged) and automatic compatibility checks for model families. 3) Exposes `rwdctl econ simulate --tenant <id> --dry-run` to run a simulation with historical traffic and get recommended batch/cache/quant defaults. 4) Telemetry: per-tenant unit-econ events, batch size histogram tags, quant-profile fallback counters, and new traces for decision points. 5) Safety: shadow-run mode (profiles applied to duplicate traffic), rollback triggers when quality regressions exceed threshold, and audit logs for profile changes.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler algorithm and unit tests - [x] Registry API + migration - [x] CLI dry-run + export - [x] Telemetry metrics + dashboards stub - [x] E2E shadow-run integration tests - [x] Docs for ops and tenant SREs - [x] Feature flags for gradual enablement

Commits (high level): - feat(scheduler): add budgeted_batch_scheduler with horizon prefill and soft-SLO enforcement - feat(registry): quant_profile_registry + migration to kvstore - feat(cli): rwdctl econ simulate and export commands - perf: small kernel selection tweak for compact int8 paths - test: add synthetic replay harness and e2e shadow-run tests - docs: add operations guide and playbook - fix: handle cold-starts and compatibility edge cases

Files/areas changed (high level): - services/scheduler/budgeted_batch_scheduler.py - services/quant/quant_profile_registry.py - cli/rwdctl/econ.py - infra/migrations/20260212_add_quant_profiles.sql - telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml - tests/integration/shadow_run_e2e.test - docs/ops/econ-playbook.md - dashboards/tenant/unit_econ_overview.json - hooks/decision_traces/trace_exporter.go - examples/sample_profiles/compact_profiles.json

Small illustrative snippets: - registry API (sketch): POST /api/v1/quant-profiles {"name": "q4f-compact-1", "base_model": "redwood/llama-like-13b", "profile": "q4f", "expected_speedup": "1.6x", "quality_delta": "0.6%"} - scheduler pseudocode: if tenant_budget_remaining < min_headroom: route_to_standard_scheduler() else: apply_budgeted_prefill()

Review conversation (summary): - Marcus Lee (reviewer): "Nice work on keeping the scheduler pure; question about metric cardinality from per-tenant unit-econ events." Author reply: "We aggregate by tenant buckets and sample heavy tenants; added a rate-limited histogram in telemetry to address cardinality." - Oliver Chen: "Can we ensure rollback triggers do not cause oscillation?" Author: "Added a 10-minute cooldown window and hysteresis on rollout percentages; documented in ops playbook." - Rina Sato: "Migration looks fine but watch for older deployments without kv migrations." Author: "Migration is additive and guarded behind feature flag; added a one-time migration job with idempotency checks." - CI bot: flagged flakiness on e2e shadow test on first run; test updated to remove timing race and re-run succeeded.

CI summary: Initial pipeline: lint -> unit tests -> integration -> e2e(shadow). First run: integration passed, e2e failed (timing race). Second run: all checks passed. Metrics/bench: microbench shows 15-28% token cost reductions on compact profiles for sampled tenants in simulation, with median tail latency increase <5ms in canary runs.

Deployment and rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag - Run `rwdctl econ simulate` for top 50 tenants to produce recommended defaults - Enable shadow-run for 72h for each tenant before canary - Canary rollout 5% traffic for 24h with automatic rollback on quality spikes - Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% once stable

Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-20 after approvals from reviewers. Follow-ups: ENG-9612 (metric cardinality heatmap), ENG-9620 (automated rollback tuning), PM-482 (tenant-facing UI to view recommended defaults).

Notes for reviewers and operators: This PR is intentionally conservative on live rollouts: default is shadow-only. The CLI dry-run is the recommended first step for tenant ops. The quant_profile_registry includes an audit log and an admin-only UI will be added in a follow-up PR.
